intro: A broken garage door spring stops your door. It can make the door heavy or prevent it from opening entirely. We fix garage door springs in Oak Park, IL. Our team replaces broken torsion and extension springs. We use high-cycle, oil-tempered torsion springs. Extension springs include safety cables. We also replace worn bearing plates and winding cones. We are a family-owned company. We offer service 24 hours a day, Monday through Saturday. You get an upfront, flat-rate quote before any work starts. Book online and save 10% on your repair. Our trucks carry common parts. This means we often complete repairs on the first visit. We test the door balance and safety reverse after every job. Your garage door will operate correctly and safely.
localContext: Oak Park’s historic garages face specific challenges. Many detached alley garages serve Architecturally Protected Victorians and Prairie-style homes in the Frank Lloyd Wright Historic District. These garages often have older, heavier carriage-house style doors. Chicago's weather, with its wide temperature swings, stresses metal springs. This makes springs wear out faster. Broken springs are common in homes across the Hemingway District and Gunderson Historic District. A spring failure can leave your vintage brick garage door stuck. This is especially true for older doors that lack proper maintenance. Owners in Oak Park want repairs that match their property's look. We ensure repairs respect the streetscape.

problemSigns.detail: This often signals a broken torsion spring. It releases a lot of energy when it snaps.

problemSigns.sign: Garage Door Won't Lift or Feels Heavy
problemSigns.detail: A broken spring means the opener struggles or fails to lift the door. Manual lifting becomes very difficult.
Look above the door. A gap in the coiled spring means it is broken. The spring will be in two pieces.

problemSigns.sign: Door Lifts a Few Inches Then Stops
problemSigns.detail: This indicates the spring system cannot support the door's weight. The opener detects resistance and stops.
Loose or slack cables on either side of the door drum usually mean a broken spring has removed tension.
